FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Steel Castings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1968 and subsequently revision is mainly to incorporate additionally the applicable draft ( taper j, so as to make it a comprehensive standard, ting the dimensions of steel castings. revised in 1976 and 1986. The present machining allowances and permissibie covering at one place all aspects affec-

Normally tolerances are specified for all important dimensions on the engineering drawings. The deviations specified in this standard relate to untoleranced dimensions of unmachincd sand and shell moulded castings. Futher machining allowances are to be added for outside dimensions and subtracted for internal dimensions. These machining allowances should not be less than the minimum machining depth necessary, plus the negative deviation in the case of outside dimensions and the positive deviation in the case of internal dimensions. In the preparation i) ISO/CD ii) Czech of this standard, assistance has been derived tolerances from the following and machining publications: allowances'.

8062 Casting Standard

System

of dimensional standard'.

CSN 014470 `Accuracy

Attention of the purchaser is invited to the fact that permissibe deviations on untoleranced dimensions vary depending upon whether the concerned steel casting involves shell moulding or machine moulding or hand moulding; so also the permissible machining allowance and draft. Apart from following the useful norm of specifying tolerances as well as permissible allowances on all important dimensions, the purchaser is advised to also stipulate in the drawing or in the enquiry and the order, the class of dimensional deviations, machining allowances and draft that he would like to be followed that is whether class lA, 1 or 2.

Indian Standard

DEVIATIONS ON UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONSANDMASSOF STEEL CASTINGS ( Third Revision )
1 SCOPE 2.1.2 Overall Dimension The largest measurable dimension of a casting or a particular part of a casting in which the nominal dimension is located. The overall dimension is to be considered in a plane normal to the nominal dimension ( see Annex A ). 2.2 Types of Dimensional Deviations 2.2.1 Positive deviation is the difference between the maximum permissible dimension and the nominal dimension. 2.2.2 Negative deviation is the between the minimum permissible and the nommal dimension. 2.3 Machining Allowance difference dimension

1.1This standard covers the following:
1.1.1 Permissible deviations on the untoleranced dimensions and mass of sand and shell moulded steel castings ( see Tables 1 to 7 ). It consists of the following 3 classes of deviations: Class IA Class 1 Class 2 Deviations for steel castings involving shell moulding Deviations for steel castings involving machine moulding Deviations for steel castings involving hand moulding

may be allowances that 1.1.2 Machining provided on faces which are subject to subsequent machining ( see Tables 8 and 9 ). 1.1.3 Permissible ( see Table 10 ). draft that may be provided

1.2 The method of classification of steel castings based on whether they are made by shell, machine or hand moulding as given in 1.1.1 would also apply for the purpose of 1.1.2 and 1.1.3. 2 TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this following definitions shall apply. 2.1 Dimensions 2.1.1 Nominal Dimension The dimension prescribed on the production drawing to which deviation is to be applied ( see Annex A ). 2.1.1.1 If the surfaces influencing a dimension are not provided with machining allowances, the nominal dimension of the final casting is the dimension specified in the drawing. 2.1.1.2 If the surfaces influencing a dimension are provided with machining allowances, then the nominal dimension on a casting is equal to the total of the dimension given in the machined component drawing and the relevant machining allowances. standard, the

This is the stock of extra material, which is provided on the relevant surface of a raw casting, on removing which, in the process of machining, the casting would attain the finish machined dimension shown in the drawing of machined component. Provision of machining allowance, and the consequent machining, are necessary wherever the `as cast' dimensional tolerances that are attainable are not close enough for a given application and require improvement by the process of machining. Machining is sometimes also done to enhance the `as cast' surface finish or to alter the shape of a casting to suit a particular application. 2.4 Draft Draft is the taper that is necessary to be provided in case of all vertical faces ( faces perpendicular to the parting plane ) in a pattern to facilitate its withdrawal from the mould. While `draft' is ordinarily understood to mean the taper provided in the patterns or core boxes for the purpose of this standard `draft' shali mean the taper found on the casting faces, which may result from either the draft in the patterns/&ore boxes, or from any other process variations.

DIMENSIONS 3.1 Permissibe deviations on the nominal dimensions of a casting shall be as given in Tables 1 to 3 respectively for the partkdar class of accuracy. 3.2 Total change in a nominal dimension due to

shift of cope and drag, change in geometrical shape or profile, warpage, rough surface, etc, and other reasons should not exceed the permissible deviations indicated by the respective class of accuracy. The same deviations shall be applicable to cover warpage or nonconformity with a given profile.

4.2 The nominal mass of a casting shall be deemed to be the average of the actual masses of a batch of castings, all of which have dimensions within the permissible deviations. 4.2.1 By prior agreement, the purchaser and the manufacturer may choose a different basis of defining the nominal mass, and also decide what will constitute a batch of castings. 5 PERMISSIBLE DEVIATIONS TO-CENTRE DISTANCE ON CENTRE-

7.2 While the values given in Tables 8 and 9 are the maximum as far as the manufacturing foundry is concerned, it is open to the purchaser to specify higher machining allowances, if he so desires, at the time of enquiry and the order. 7.3 The interpretation of providing machining allowance, and its relationship with the casting tolerances ( as specified in Tables 1, 2 and 3 ) are as illustrated in Fig. la, b, c and d. It is to be noted that a machining allowance specified in Tables 8 and 9 1s the nominal maximum amount that would survive in spite of there occurring the maximum perqisslble negative deviation in case of an external dimension ( see Fig. 1 a ), or the maximum possibJt gqsitive deviation in case of an internal dimension ( see Fig. I b ). Hence, a particular casting may give a total machining stock, for example, in case of an internal stirface, equal to the machining allowance specified in Table 8 plus the maximum negative deviation permissible in accordance with Tables ~1; .2 and 3. as the case may be ( as applicable to that face based on the interpretation given in Fig. la ), plus the permissible draft in accordance with Table 10. Thus, when it is stated that a machining allowance given in Tables 8 or 9 is the maximum, it means that it is the maximum value allowed over and above the corresponding applicable dimensional deviation as per Tables 1, 2 or 3 plus the corresponding applicable draft as per Table 10. 4

NOTES R = Raw casting dimension; F = Finished dimension; M.4 - Machine allowance ( see 2.3 and 7 ); CT = Casting tolerance range as per Table 1, 2 or 3; and D = Draft ( see 2.4 aud 8 ) ( in this illustration SD represents the +ve draft as referred to in 8.3 and 8.4 ). FIG. 1 ILLUSTRATION OF MACHINING ALLOWANCEAND ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH CASING TOLERANCE AND DRAPE

7.3.1 If a surface requiring machining has a linkage or a reference with more than one point or surface, then the greater distance shall be taken as the nominal dimension for the purpose of deriving the applicable machining allowance. 7.4 Once it is prescribed that the specified machining allowance represents the amount of machining stock over and above the applicable dimensional deviation, it is no longer necessary to distinguish between machine moulding and 5

hand moulding for specifying the machining allowances. Hence Table 9 covers all sand castings, made by either machine moulding or hand moulding. However, in case of shell moulded casting the outer skin of the metal is relativJy less rough and more clean than that of ordinary sand castings, and hence a lesser amount of machining stock need only be removed to reach the clean inner layer. In view of this, a separate set of values covering the permissible machining allowance for this group of castings is specified in Table 8.

IS4891:1994 SDRAFI' 8.1The maximum permissible
8.4.1 f ve Draft - This type of draft is used where the design of a casting does not allow an increase or decrease of the nominal dimension more than ,20 percent of the specified value of the draft, over and above the applicable dimensional deviation. 8.4.2 + ve Draft - This type of draft is most commonly used and is applicable wherever the concerned face is machined or where it is not machined but the casting.design and application permit an increase in the nominal dimension in case of an external surface,- and a decrease in case of an internal surface. 8.4.3 -ve Draft - This type of draft is used where the concerned casting surface remains unmachined and the casting design and the application do not permit an increase in the concerned nominal dimension in case of an external surface, and a decrease in case of an internal surface. 8.5 A purchaser is free to indicate, preferably in the drawing, his choice concerning the kind of draft that may be provided. However, if not thus specified at the time of enquiry and the order, the manufacturer is free to use his discretion concerning the type of draft to be used during pattern making. 9 GENERAL In view of the foregoing, the total permissible change in a given nominal dimension of a casting would be the sum of the permissible deviation on the dimension in accordance with Tables 1, 2 and 3, the applicable machining allowance in accordance with Tables 8 and 9, and the permissible draft in accordance with Table 10.

draft per surface

shall be as given in Table 10. 8.2, While it, is theoretically possible in most cases to eliminate the draft by surrounding a given vertical surface with a core, this method is as it would substantially largely unfeasible, raise the costs. Thus in case of practically all a certain degree exposed vertical faces, of draft becomes unavoidable. The quantum of such a draft would vary depending upon of the vertical face, not only the height but also based upon such other factors as ood, plastic, whether the pattern is made of e of moulding or metal, its surface finish, the ty p" sand and process used, etc. While it would be logical from the foundry point of view to account for ail these factors in specifying the permissible draft, it would not be reasonable to expect a purchaser of castings to be familiar with all such aspects and ,be uncertain of the amount of draft the castings bought by him may actually have, depending on such factors. Hence, as a measure of simplification and avoiding contradiction, a distinction is made on the permissible extent of draft for a given height based only on the moulding process, which distinction has already been the basis of differentiating between Tables 1, 2 and 3. The Table 10 for draft is drawn up accordingly. 8.3 The draft provided can be of any of the following 3 types: f ve, + Ye, or - Ye This differentiation is illustrated in Fig. 2a, 2b and 2c. 8.4 The following basis is ordinarily followed in choosing the type of draft.
